reason: E1 shows that FeCoNiMnCu forms a protective Cr2O3 and spinel layer after thermal exposure and that harder phases increase hardness, but it provides no evidence on mechanical disruption of the film, repassivation kinetics, or the dynamic balance governing tribo-corrosion. The key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: FeCoNiMnCu HEA can form a protective Cr2O3 layer and high-entropy spinel upon thermal exposure
The formed oxide/spinel layer is mechanically robust enough to affect wear behavior
The oxide film can be mechanically disrupted by sliding wear, exposing reactive metal
The exposed alloy surface can repassivate by reforming the oxide film
The dynamic balance between film removal and repassivation governs tribo-corrosion degradation
